fields.notes:
He was a devotee of Lord Gaurāṅga (Nāmāmṛta-samudra 159, ed. Haridāsa Dāsa).

The record also held Akiñcana Dāsa the translator of the Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He translated in verse the Śrī Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka (Calcutta University manuscript no. 1512). Taken out of the record «Akiñcana Dāsa» #25, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Ānanda Dāsa (author of the Jagadīśa-caritra)
fields.notes:
Fifth generation of the line of Jagadīśa Paṇḍita. In a dream Bhāgavatānanda, a disciple of one of Jagadīśa Paṇḍita's disciples, told him to write the Śrī Jagadīśa-caritra, compiled in 1640-50 Śaka (1718-1728 A.D.).

The record also held Ānanda Dāsa the disciple of Śyāmānandī Dāmodara, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Śyāmānandī Dāmodara (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 15.18). Taken out of the record «Ānanda Dāsa» #34, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a descendant in the disciple line of Advaita Prabhu (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.61).

The record also held Ananta Dāsa the poet, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
A Vaiṣṇava poet: the Padakalpataru has 32 padas with the bhaṇitā of Ananta dāsa (Baṅgīya Sāhitya Sevaka). Taken out of the record «Ananta Dāsa» #45, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

A brāhmaṇa of Navadvīpa and a disciple of Advaita Prabhu; in Kṛṣṇa-līlā Sudevī. The Padakalpataru has one pada of «Ananta» (Vaiṣṇava-vandanā of Jīva Gosvāmī, Devakīnandana and Vṛndāvana dāsa; Bhakti Movement in Orissa p. 173). Which Ananta composed the padas is not known: Ananta Ācārya, Ananta dāsa or Ananta Paṇḍita.

The text on Ananta Ācārya (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.58) went to his record #44 (07-11-2026).

A devotee from Orissa and close companion of Nityānanda Prabhu (Vaiṣṇava-vandanā).

The record also held the Balarāma Dāsa of Caitanya-bhāgavata 3.5.734 and Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.34, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).

A devotee of Nityānanda's branch mentioned in Caitanya-bhāgavata 3.5.734 and Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.34. Taken out of the record «Balarāma Dās (Mahānta)» #77, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu; his Śrīpāṭa is at Budhuri (Prema-vilāsa 20).

The record also held the Balarāma Kavipati disciple of Rāmacandra Kavirāja, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Rāmacandra Kavirāja (Karṇānanda 2). Taken out of the record «Balarāma Kavipati» #83, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Bhadravatī (mother of Jāhnavā)
fields.notes:
She was the wife of Sūryadāsa Paṇḍita and the mother of Jāhnavā.

The record also held Bhadravatī the mother of Uddhāraṇa Datta, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
She was the mother of Uddhāraṇa Datta Ṭhākura and the wife of Śrīkara Datta (see «Uddhāraṇa Datta»). Taken out of the record «Bhadravati» #95, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala 14.107).

The record also held three other Bhagavāns of the Rasikamaṅgala (14.119-129, 14.142, 14.148), now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was the nephew and disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala 14.119-129). Taken out of the record «Bhagavān» #103, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple in Rasikānanda Prabhu's line (Rasikamaṅgala 14.142). Taken out of the record «Bhagavān» #103, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple in Rasikānanda Prabhu's line (Rasikamaṅgala 14.148). Taken out of the record «Bhagavān» #103, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura (Narottama-vilāsa 12).

The record also held the Bhakta Dāsa disciple of Rasikānanda, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.150). Taken out of the record «Bhakta Dās» #116, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.114).

The record also held another Bhūdhara, disciple of Rasikānanda (14.152), now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
Another disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu named Bhūdhara (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.152). Taken out of the record «Bhudhara» #149, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Brahmānanda (brother of Nityānanda)
fields.notes:
He was the younger brother of Nityānanda Prabhu (Prema-vilāsa 24).

The record also held the Brahmānanda of Lord Gaurāṅga's kīrtana at Navadvīpa, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).

He took part in Lord Gaurāṅga's kīrtana at Navadvīpa (Caitanya-bhāgavata 2.8.116, 2.18.9, 102-107, 2.28.12, 104, 3.2.35). Taken out of the record «Brahmananda» #163, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Darpanārāyaṇa
fields.notes:
He wrote the Śrī Kṛṣṇa-cautiśā (Baṅgīya Sāhitya Sevaka).

The record also held the Darpanārāyaṇa disciple of Hemalatā Devī, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
He was a disciple of Hemalatā Devī, the daughter of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya Prabhu (Karṇānanda 2). Taken out of the record «Darpanarayana» #190, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

A brāhmaṇa of Śāligrāma, the fifth son of Kaṁsāri Miśra; Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita and Sūryadāsa Paṇḍita were his brothers. He composed many padas in praise of his elder brother Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita, with the bhaṇitā «Dīna Kṛṣṇa Dāsa».

The record also held the Oḍiyā poet Dīna Kṛṣṇa Dāsa, author of the Rasakallola, now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
An Oḍiyā poet, author of the Rasakallola: thirty-four prosodic styles, on the musical rāgas and rāgiṇīs. Taken out of the record «Dīna Kṛṣṇa Dāsa» #220, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Dvija Gopīmohana
fields.notes:
He was a disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.156).

The record also held another Gopīmohana, disciple of Rasikānanda (14.127), now in a record of its own (07-11-2026).
Another disciple of Rasikānanda Prabhu named Gopīmohana (Rasikamaṅgala Paścima 14.127). Taken out of the record «Dvija Gopimohana» #248, which mixed several persons (07-11-2026).
